title: Invertibility locus of an endomorphism of an exact functor
statement: Let $A,B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], let $G:A\to B$ be additive and preserve finite limits and finite colimits, and let $\alpha:G\to G$ be a natural transformation. For every $g:M\to N$ such that $\alpha_M$ and $\alpha_N$ are isomorphisms, the components $\alpha_{\ker g}$, $\alpha_{\operatorname{coker}g}$ and $\alpha_{\operatorname{im}g}$ are isomorphisms. For every short exact sequence $0\to M\to P\to N\to0$ such that $\alpha_M$ and $\alpha_N$ are isomorphisms, $\alpha_P$ is an isomorphism. There is no assertion about arbitrary subobjects.

proof.text: Preservation of kernels conjugates the component at a kernel to the induced kernel map of the naturality square. Its inverse is induced by the inverse endpoint maps. The dual cokernel argument is identical; these are Mathlib kernel.map and cokernel.map isomorphism instances.
Apply cokernel closure to the kernel inclusion, then transport across the canonical abelian coimage-image isomorphism by naturality.
Map the short exact sequence by G. The naturality diagram has invertible outside arrows, so [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma] proves invertibility of the middle arrow.

lean.statement:
theorem exactEndomorphism_iso_closure :
    (∀ (M N : A) (g : M ⟶ N), IsIso (α.app M) → IsIso (α.app N) →
      IsIso (α.app (kernel g)) ∧ IsIso (α.app (cokernel g)) ∧
        IsIso (α.app (image g))) ∧
    (∀ S : ShortComplex A, S.ShortExact → IsIso (α.app S.X₁) →
      IsIso (α.app S.X₃) → IsIso (α.app S.X₂))
